rows.note: HARNESS DEFECT, not an artifact defect. dispatch-gate.sh sets `set -uo pipefail` (line 11) and then tests large payloads with `printf '%s' "$var" | grep -q PATTERN`. grep -q exits on first match, printf takes SIGPIPE (141), and pipefail promotes 141 to pipeline failure -- so a REAL MATCH is reported as no-match, racily, whenever the payload outlives grep's exit. Measured on INVARIANTS.md (44458-byte NON-NEGOTIABLES slice) with byte-identical inputs (INVARIANTS.md 435b5b76, .forge-state.json 497ea8f3) across 20 consecutive runs: 13 pass_with_blockers, 4 'has no numbered rows', 3 'names no judge's attack'. Isolated loop without pipefail: 0/400 failures; with pipefail: 3/400. Blast radius: 11 sites in dispatch-gate.sh (981, 1655, 1656, 1679, 1962, 2303, 2412, 2467, 2693, 2721, 2762) and ~50 sibling sites across utils/ (forge-scope-kickoff.sh 13, phase-model-dispatch.sh 4, craft-lint.sh 4, closure-reverify.sh 4, anti-gaming-gate.sh 3, ...), nearly all under pipefail. POLARITY MATTERS: `... | grep -q X || fail` (1655/1656) can only FALSE-NEGATIVE -> a spurious fail, fail-closed and noisy; but `... && printf | grep -qF` (2412) FAILS OPEN -> a SIGPIPE turns a non-match into a vacuous PASS. The fail-open half is the same vacuous-pass defect class as the out-of-enum state strings this redo already fixed. Semantics-preserving fix is a herestring (`grep -qE PATTERN <<< "$var"`), bash-3.2-safe.
